prompt: Create a polished desktop web experience design comp for 'aureole', an interactive real-time particle art showcase. Render a complete edge-to-edge 16:9 screen with crisp readable interface text, no browser/device surround. The visitor explores three scenes and adjusts light and motion. This comp shows 'The current': an immense diagonal, curling river made of countless individual tiny gold, amber, crimson and occasional jade particles, sweeping from lower left through the center to upper right, with flowing filaments, deep black negative space, restrained HDR bloom, sharp glittering midground and soft foreground bokeh. Think cinematic Foundation title-sequence atmosphere, richly dimensional granular light, never flat neon lines or simple stars. Main artwork fills the screen. A small elegant 'aureole' wordmark sits top left with 'Studies in light & matter'; unobtrusive 'Cinema view' top right. Lower left heading 'The current' with subtitle 'A river of light, finding its own way.' A bottom navigation rail selects '01 Current / Flow field', '02 Relic / Matter & form', '03 Continuum / Recursive lattice'. Current is active with a fine gold line. Bottom right compact pause, 'Auto journey', settings, and save-frame controls. Bottom edge small 'AN EXPERIMENT IN PARTICLE LIGHT', 'Move to disturb · Drag to orbit'. Use refined light-weight modern sans typography in warm ivory, hairline separators, restrained spacious controls; artwork dominates without text obscuring its luminous heart. This is a working web interface comp, not a poster.
